boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented settings for independent work, tutoring, writing help, group sessions and residence-hall study, with access limits noted.

cards.title: Settle In With Research Tools Close By
cards.subtitle: Public workstations, study rooms and academic services
cards.notes: Start research here when you need a workstation, database access or a small room; ask library staff about current room availability.
cards.short_summary: A resource-rich base for research, computer work and focused sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding states that Brackett Library offers more than 60 public workstations, conference rooms, small study rooms and almost 200 online databases.
cards.source_title: Brackett Library | Catalog, Archives & Research | Harding
cards.access_notes: Library services are offered to Harding's student body. Consult the library's current website or staff for building hours and study-room availability.

cards.title: Bring a Draft and Work Through the Sticking Point
cards.subtitle: First floor of Brackett Library
cards.notes: Schedule help for planning, research, revision or citation formatting; walk in only when staffing permits and bring the assignment prompt.
cards.short_summary: A staffed setting for turning an unfinished paper into a workable revision plan.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding identifies the Writing Center at the back of Brackett Library's first floor and says it assists with planning, research, organization, revision and citation formats.
cards.source_title: Writing Center | Help with Essays, Grammar and Formatting | Harding
cards.access_notes: Appointments are encouraged; walk-ins are accepted as staffing allows. Posted hours are Sunday 6-10 p.m., Monday-Thursday 1-10 p.m. and Friday 1-4 p.m.

cards.title: Use the Lounge for a Conversational Work Session
cards.subtitle: Shared seating inside Hammon Student Center
cards.notes: Choose this lounge for discussion-friendly work or a project check-in; use headphones and shift elsewhere when you need quiet concentration.
cards.short_summary: A social indoor setting suited to collaborative work between campus commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding's current undergraduate handbook documents a student lounge area in Hammon Student Center for meeting with others.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared student-center lounge. No reservation rule or separate lounge hours are stated on the cited page; follow posted building access.

cards.title: Pair Study Time With Tutoring or Academic Coaching
cards.subtitle: Hammon Student Center, second floor, room 236
cards.notes: Come with a specific course problem or study habit to address; contact the center before arriving to confirm tutoring or coaching arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A support-centered environment for guided course work and learning strategies.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding locates the Academic Resource Center in Student Center room 236 and documents individual tutoring, group Supplemental Instruction and academic coaching.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Hammon Student Center in room 236. Contact the ARC for current tutoring, coaching and Supplemental Instruction schedules.

cards.title: Take Focused Work to the Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Resident study lounge in Armstrong Hall
cards.notes: Use the second-floor lounge when your room is distracting; verify resident access with the hall staff and keep the shared space orderly.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated residence-hall alternative to studying at a bedroom desk.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding's current residence-life page identifies a second-floor study lounge among Armstrong Hall's common areas and amenities.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall space; intended for eligible Armstrong Hall residents. Ask the RLC or RA about access and any current lounge rules.

cards.title: Pick Soft Seating on the Second or Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Two resident lounges with soft seating
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work that fits soft seating; residents can compare the second- and third-floor rooms before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Two furnished resident spaces designed for a change of scene within the hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding documents study lounges with soft seating on both the second and third floors of Cathcart Hall.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall spaces for eligible Cathcart Hall residents. The building has no elevator; consult the RLC or RA about current access rules.

cards.title: Move Upstairs for a Dedicated Study Setting
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor resident lounges
cards.notes: Head upstairs with a defined task and the materials you need; check with hall staff before inviting anyone who does not live in Harbin.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated upper-floor rooms that separate study from the busier first-floor lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding lists study lounges on the second and third floors of Harbin Hall among the building's common amenities.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall spaces for eligible Harbin Hall residents. The building has no elevator; ask the RLC or RA about guests and current use rules.

cards.title: Choose a Study Floor With Elevator Access
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor resident lounges
cards.notes: Use either upper-floor lounge for routine coursework; take the elevator if needed and confirm guest or group-use expectations with staff.
cards.short_summary: Two resident study options connected by an elevator-equipped building.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding documents second- and third-floor study lounges in Sears Hall and states that the building has an elevator.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall spaces for eligible Sears Hall residents. Consult the RLC or RA for current access, guest and shared-space requirements.

cards.title: Shift From the Lobby to an Upper-Floor Lounge
cards.subtitle: Resident study rooms on floors two and three
cards.notes: Take individual or small-group work upstairs; residents should confirm current quiet expectations and leave shared seating ready for others.
cards.short_summary: Two dedicated study areas away from Allen Hall's multipurpose first-floor lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding lists a study lounge on both the second and third floors of Allen Hall and notes that the building has an elevator.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall spaces for eligible Allen Hall residents. Ask the RLC or RA about current lounge access and guest policies.

cards.title: Use Either Upper Floor for a Study Reset
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor resident lounges
cards.notes: Relocate here when you need separation from your room; pack everything first because the official listing notes there is no elevator.
cards.short_summary: A pair of resident study rooms reached from Keller Hall's upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding's residence-life page identifies study lounges on Keller Hall's second and third floors and notes that the building has no elevator.
cards.source_title: Residence Life, Dorms and Apartments | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall spaces for eligible Keller Hall residents. The building has no elevator; consult the RLC or RA about current access rules.
